159842.overview: Oricmunch is a Pac-Man variant with more or less identical gameplay as the original. The player controls the Oricmuncher and has to navigate his way through a maze and eat all the dots that lay ahead of him. At the same time he has to watch out for the ghosts that roam the corridors. If a ghost catches him he will lose a life. To attack the ghosts the player has to eat a special item which will charge him for a short while. While charged he can then go after the ghosts and eat them. The game has nine levels with different maze layouts, colors and difficulty that can be either played through in order or picked from the beginning. The player advances a level when he has either eaten all the dots or all the ghosts.

175613.overview: Oric Trek is a conversion of the old mainframe Star Trek game for the Oric computers. It was developed and released by Salamander Software in 1983.

175856.overview: You must defend the earth from hordes of bomb dropping space invaders, using your earth bound laser base. The more invaders you hit, the faster they come, leading to a gun-blazing shootout finale.

175871.overview: Let the computer set up the board for you, enjoy a nice, satisfying game of backgammon with Orical Backgammon. Created by R. Buckley and A. Birds for Dormere Software and released in 1983.

175872.overview: You are in command of Lunar defence station #4, your task, to defend th e4 lunar reactor pods vital to earth's existence. You have 3 mobile missile bases to destroy the waves of invading aliens.

175927.overview: A space-invaders type game with different opponents, that try to avoid the bullets fired at them.

215842.overview: Orioc Golf (also known as 48K Oric Golf) is a simple golf game for the Oric Atmos/Oric-1 computers. It has up to six players, and the players have a choice of playing either 9 holes or 18 holes. It was developed and published by R & R Software in 1983.

215861.overview: Asteroids (also called Oric Meteors in-game) is a clone of the arcade classic space rock blasting shmup of the same name for the Oric-1 and Atmos computers. It was developed and released by Arctic Computing in 1983.

215862.overview: Awari is a computerized version of an ancient African board game that is known under several names, including the title of this game. The game was developed and published by Kenema Associates Ltd in 1983.

423559.overview: Bandit (also called One Arm Bandit in-game) is a fruit machines simulation for the Oric-1/Oric Atmos line of computers. It was developed by Tansoft and published by Express Software in 1983.
